name: US jobless claims
summary: US initial jobless claims rose to 200,000 in the week to 7 Nov; 4-week average 195,250, at its 52-week low
state: Initial US jobless claims rose 9,000 to 200,000 in the week to 7 Nov, above forecasts of 195,000, after an upward revision to 191,000 the week before (Labor Department via ANI, 12 Nov). The four-week average was unchanged at 195,250, at or within 1% of its 52-week low and far below the 15% Watch line. Continuing claims fell 20,000 to 1.697 million.
for_you: Layoffs remain low. Workers in rate-sensitive sectors are the most exposed if higher borrowing costs start to slow hiring.
rubric_hit: Normal: 4-week average 195,250 is under 1% above its 52-week low, below the 15% Watch line

sources.title: ANI — US initial jobless claims climb to 200,000, four-week average remains unchanged

why: Weekly claims are the earliest hard data on US layoffs; a sustained rise usually comes before the unemployment rate turns.
drivers: Layoffs, hiring freezes, federal job cuts, storms, strikes and seasonal quirks.

rubric.normal: The 4-week average of initial claims is less than 15% above its 52-week low.
